memory_update.text: SENEA should be tracked as a direct underfollowed private-label/co-pack food manufacturing candidate for value-retail and grocery private-brand expansion.
PACK should be tracked as a second-order packaging and automation candidate, but its private-label linkage requires customer/channel verification.
SPSC should be tracked as an operational-plumbing candidate for retailer-supplier integration and compliance, not as a direct product manufacturer.
WMT is the key reference demand anchor for private-brand volume, formulation changes, packaging requirements, and supplier qualification pressure.

Need a later pass focused specifically on micro-cap and sub-$300M formulation/contract-manufacturing exceptions such as supplement and OTC/private-label manufacturers; exclude unless liquidity and customer concentration are explicitly mapped.

node: Private-label, contract manufacturing, packaging, and formulation for consumer staples and value retail
summary: Layer 1B expands the direct public-company universe around value-retail private label and contract-manufacturing capacity. The reference lane uses Walmart as the demand anchor because its private-brand push creates volume and qualification pressure on suppliers. The underfollowed lane prioritizes Seneca Foods as a scaled private-label/co-pack food processor, Ranpak as a packaging-equipment and consumables supplier to e-commerce/industrial supply chains, and SPS Commerce as the retail-supplier integration and compliance network that may become more valuable as private-label supplier complexity rises. These are research candidates only, not recommendations.
